facility_roles.quote: The "Troitsk nu-mass" program is conducted by the Institute for Nuclear Research of the Russian Academy of Sciences.

intervals.label: tritium beta-decay neutrino-mass measurements
intervals.note: Year precision, from the group's own 2015 status paper. The data set analysed in the final neutrino-mass paper (PRD 84, 112003) was 'acquired from 1994 to 2004'; the broader 1985-2005 range counts the whole measurement programme.
intervals.quote: The corresponding measurements were done from 1985 to 2005 [24, 25] and the final results of these efforts were published in [19].

intervals.label: proposal of the keV sterile-neutrino search at the Troitsk nu-mass facility
intervals.note: Start is the arXiv v1 date (2015-04-02) of the paper proposing a new experiment at the existing facility; end is the arXiv v1 date of the first-measurements paper (2017-03-31). Neither is an approval or construction date.
intervals.quote: We propose a new experiment to search for a sterile neutrino in a few keV mass range at the "Troitsk nu-mass" facility.

intervals.label: keV sterile-neutrino search: first measurements and continued operation
intervals.note: Start is the arXiv v1 date of the paper reporting the first measurements (the measurements themselves are older, undated in the abstract). The interval is open because no source consulted says the measurements have stopped; the most recent dated evidence found is that 2017 paper (a conference abstract mentions a planned TRISTAN-Troitsk upgrade), so current operation on 2026-10-26 is not confirmed.
intervals.quote: We present the first measurements of tritium beta-decay spectrum in the electron energy range 16-18.6 keV.

quantity.note: One of three limit estimates in the abstract: sensitivity limit 2.2 eV, Bayesian 2.12 eV, Feldman-Cousins 2.05 eV (all 95% CL).
quantity.quote: This gives an experimental upper sensitivity limit of mν < 2.2 eV , 95% C . L. and upper limit estimates mν < 2.12 eV , 95% C .L. for Bayesian statistics and mν < 2.05 eV , 95% C .L. for the Feldman and Cousins approach.

name: Troitsk nu-mass
notes: Date conflict: the group's 2015 paper dates the measurements 1985-2005, while the final-results paper analyses a data set 'acquired from 1994 to 2004'; the broader range is recorded as the interval and the narrower in its note.
No official website was found. The hull has a gap between 2005 and the 2015 proposal (no data taking is recorded in that period; the 2011-2013 papers re-analyse the old data).
KATRIN lineage: the predecessor row lives on experiment:katrin.

physics_goals.quote: with a goal to limit the mass of electron anti-neutrino by analyzing the shape of tritium beta decay spectrum near the end point
physics_goals.value: Limit the mass of the electron antineutrino from the shape of the tritium beta-decay spectrum near its endpoint

physics_goals.quote: The goal is to find distortions which may correspond to the presence of a heavy sterile neutrinos.
physics_goals.value: Search for keV-mass sterile neutrinos as a kink in the tritium beta spectrum

summary.plain: A tritium beta-decay experiment near Moscow that weighed the electron antineutrino by measuring the electron spectrum with an electrostatic filter. Its final analysis limits the mass to about 2.2 electron-volts; the same setup now hunts for keV sterile neutrinos.
summary.technical: Windowless gaseous tritium source and an integrating electrostatic MAC-E spectrometer (resolution 3-4 eV) at INR RAS, Troitsk; measurements 1985-2005 (final analysis of 1994-2004 data: m² = -0.67 ± 2.53 eV², m(νe) < 2.2 eV sensitivity limit) and, from 2017, keV-sterile-neutrino searches.
